name: srsvd-ooc-throughput.goal_cast
purpose: Campaign-specific two-worker cast for .goal/srsvd-ooc-throughput.json, derived from .goal/base.goal_cast.json (left untouched). Shape: 'beat the current best record' where the record is STEADY5_GB on the fixed 1.546 TB out-of-core store on one L40S. One implementer, one runner, orchestrator absorbs the skeptic and the method (time budget -> T_min -> gap -> lever order -> re-measure). Nothing here overrides the contract; the contract text is authoritative and this file mirrors its operating_mode for reuse.
assumes: 2-4 delegations per regular iteration (1-3 implementers, opus/xhigh, plus 1 runner, opus/medium); a SETUP PHASE of at most 3 iterations with 1-4 workers of any shape and no candidate; at least 100 iterations; stop after 300 turns; claims file, scoreboard and setup file on. Differences from base.goal_cast.json: implementer count 1-3 (base: exactly 1), explicit setup phase, campaign-specific metric/eligibility/protocols. base.goal_cast.json itself is unchanged.
metric: STEADY5_GB = store bytes of blocks whose device result was confirmed ready between window_open and window_close, normalised to exactly 300 s (bytes x 300 / span). window_open = first block confirmation after warm-up AND >= 32 blocks streamed; window_close = first block confirmation at or after window_open + 300.0 s; both instants are a block_until_ready on every outstanding block; span must lie in [300.0, 302.0]. If the job completes inside the window, the next identical job starts IMMEDIATELY in the same process (same pool, no re-pin, no recompile); the process runs until the window has closed AND >= 1 full job has completed with its gate printed. compiles_in_wall must be 0 over the window. Harness version H1 is FROZEN once the origin is measured; any change is H2 and re-baselines origin and champion in the same iteration.
record_eligibility: fixed store on /lscratch; ONE L40S by UUID with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES printed, ECC clean; mode direct; k=32 p=10 q=2 seed 0 (3 passes); gate PASS (G1 1e-4, G2 1e-3, G3 1e-2, G4 5e-2 two-sided) on >= 1 complete job in-process; compiles_in_wall == 0; unprofiled; both installed SHAs printed from inside the job and equal to the claimed commits; harness H1 (or current re-baselined); same-iteration champion control; margin > noise floor and >= 1 pct. Numerics-affecting (wire dtype, matmul precision, accumulation dtype) eligible if the gate passes, labelled. Never eligible: fewer passes / changed q,k,p; any dtype ON DISK; buffered / page cache; > 1 card; another tier; profiled.

operating_mode.role: You are the orchestrator. Each iteration (= one turn): think, decide what to try next, delegate to the two workers, integrate, ledger, scoreboard. Every decision is yours — workers execute and report, they never decide what to try next. YOU HOLD THE RECORD: the ledger names the current champion (code SHAs of BOTH repos + exact flags/command + its verified STEADY5_GB + the run id and node it was measured on). A candidate replaces the champion only after the runner has measured it AND the champion control in the same iteration AND you have read the raw STEADY5 rows yourself AND the margin exceeds the noise floor. A worker's report is provenance 'inherited' until you re-verify the artifact yourself; re-verify anything a later iteration will stand on. THERE IS NO SKEPTIC IN THIS CAST, so you do that job before you believe a result: does the number move in the direction the change predicted, is it too big or too small to be true (nothing on one card beats the NVMe plateau x 300 s; nothing without fewer wire bytes beats the PCIe roof), do the books balance (bytes_consumed == blocks x block bytes; span in [300, 302]; jobs_completed x 4.6386 TB consistent with bytes), and could the check this claim passed have failed at all. Record that answer in the ledger beside the claim. YOU RUN THE METHOD: after the origin and after every coronation, print the time budget over the window (H2D busy / kernel busy / read wait / idle from the phase clock or an nsys twin), the T_min terms and the binding term per .ai/research/performance-optimization-method.json, and the gap — a time budget more than one champion old is fiction. EVERYTHING THIS CAMPAIGN PRODUCES IS UNDER GIT and you check it: no candidate enters the scoreboard without commit SHAs you can `git show`. PREFER THE WORKFLOW TOOL over the Agent tool whenever Workflow is available — the cast sets reasoning effort per role and effort is settable only through Workflow. THE USER'S APPROVAL OF THIS CONTRACT AUTHORIZES THE WORKFLOW TOOL FOR DELEGATION. The cast below is mirrored in .goal/srsvd-ooc-throughput.goal_cast.json for reuse; this contract's text is authoritative.
operating_mode.cast: implementer(s) — model opus, effort xhigh; ONE TO THREE per iteration, FIRST (one is the norm; two or three only when the orchestrator judges the change large enough to split — the count is a decision recorded in the ledger). When several run, EITHER each builds a SEPARATE candidate with its own id, prediction and commit, committed sequentially through an explicit gate so one writer holds each git index at a time, and the runner measures each against ONE shared control that iteration; OR they split ONE large candidate by disjoint file ownership and the orchestrator names the integrating implementer who lands the single commit. Either way every candidate is exactly one commit pair and one prediction. Each implementer: given the current champion (SHAs, flags, STEADY5_GB, time budget and gap), the ledger's record of what has been tried and failed, and the null/harmful list, implement ONE new candidate aimed at beating the record — a code change on branch ooc-throughput in work/srsvd-jax and/or work/srsvd-jax-bench, or a flag-only change (then the artifact is the command line and the SHAs are the champion's). State the MECHANISM (which term of the time budget it attacks and why that term is the binding one or the serialised one) and the PREDICTED STEADY5_GB or band BEFORE the runner touches it. COMMIT AND PUSH: land every touched file on ooc-throughput with a message naming the iteration and candidate id, and hand back both commit SHAs, `git status --porcelain` proving both trees clean, `git show --stat`, the full patch, the exact bench command, and an explicit list of what was NOT done or NOT checked. DO NOT run the experiment, DO NOT report a score. During the SETUP PHASE (iterations 1-3 at most, each declared SETUP in the ledger) an implementer builds harness H1 (the window, block-confirmation timestamps, in-process job loop, STEADY5-ROW printer, nvidia-smi sampling hook, --steady-window-s flag) as the ONLY change on top of whole-job HEAD, so the origin is whole-job code under H1; setup workers of other shapes (allocation holder, store generator, card screener, tier prober) are allowed in those iterations. | runner — model opus, effort medium; cadence: every iteration, AFTER the implementer's commit lands. Check out / install the implementer's COMMIT SHAs into $W/.venv-cand (--reinstall --no-deps, both packages at explicit @sha) and print both direct_url.json files from INSIDE the Slurm step (srun --jobid=<id> --ntasks=1 --gres=gpu:10 with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=GPU-<uuid> pinning the record card). Run the candidate EXACTLY as specified with --steady-window-s 300, sampling nvidia-smi (SM clock, power, throttle reasons; NVML ignores CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES so filter by UUID, never index) every 5 s during the window, and in the SAME allocation on the SAME card under the SAME protocol re-run the CHAMPION from $W/.venv-champ at its own recorded SHAs and flags as the control. Report REAL MEASURED RESULTS ONLY: the full STEADY5-ROW line of each run (iter, candidate id, both SHAs, node, job id, GPU UUID, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, tier, store path and bytes, ratio to RealMemory, flags, window_open/close, span, blocks_consumed, passes_completed, jobs_completed, bytes_consumed, STEADY5_GB, STEADY5_GBps, compiles_in_wall, gate verdict with each gate's value and BINDING flag, exit code, sampled clock/power/throttle), the banner, and any nondeterminism seen. COMMIT what you produced into work/srsvd-ooc-results/iterNN/ (raw logs, STEADY5 rows, JSON, exact command lines) and hand back that commit SHA. YOU DO NOT FIX THE CANDIDATE: if it fails to install or run, report the failure verbatim with the shortest reproducing command, commit the failing log, and stop. Report what was NOT measured as explicitly as what was. Work in batches of 1 timed run: run, write its row and log, commit, then the next; never hold two results uncommitted. With several candidates in one iteration, run them serially on the same card and measure the control ONCE in that iteration, after or between them (say which). When the allocation is new (first iteration, or after expiry), the runner ALSO regenerates the store, screens all ten cards, prints the environment block, and re-measures the champion once before any candidate — those are extra items in the same batch discipline.
operating_mode.discipline: PREDICT BEFORE YOU MEASURE: the implementer's predicted STEADY5_GB goes into that iteration's ledger 'predictions' block BEFORE the runner starts; a post-hoc band proves nothing. | GIT TRACKS EVERYTHING, AND NOTHING UNCOMMITTED IS MEASURED: every source change, script, config, raw log and result file is committed on the named branch (code) or in work/srsvd-ooc-results (results) with a message naming its iteration; the runner measures COMMIT SHAs, never a dirty tree; both workers print `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain`; the pre-campaign HEAD SHAs (9a1f214 lib, 67d94db bench) are recorded in iteration 1. | CHAMPION AND CANDIDATE ARE MEASURED UNDER THE SAME CONDITIONS IN THE SAME ITERATION on the same card at their own SHAs; a record compared against a number carried from another allocation or another card is not a comparison. | THE NOISE FLOOR HAS TEETH: established in iteration 1 from >= 3 fresh origin processes (max minus min, as a fraction of the median), re-established on every new allocation; a candidate below the floor, or under 1 pct, is a NULL and is recorded as such. | SEPARATION OF DUTY: whoever writes the solution does not report its score; do not merge the two workers to save a delegation. | ONE WRITER PER SCARCE RESOURCE (the allocation, the card, the pool, each git index, each venv, the store): the implementer owns the code repos' index while committing; the runner owns the node and the results repo; Slurm serialises steps anyway. Pipelining (runner measuring N-1 while the implementer writes N) is allowed and must be declared in the ledger and the scoreboard note. | UNVERIFIED CLAIMS HAVE NO STANDING: a candidate whose rows you could not reconcile does not become champion and is not a premise later. | THE METHOD IS THE PROCESS: attribute seconds inside the window before choosing the next lever; take the highest-leverage lever that fits the branch the gap names; NULL and HARMFUL levers already measured by whole-job (depth, chunks, --h2d pinned, read-chunk 64M/256M null; lockstep, --threads 32, block-rows 2048 without register harmful; readahead and larger blocks anti-combine with register) are not retried without a new mechanism argued in the ledger.
operating_mode.delegation_guard: BASELINE: sibling agents doing the same job are a free control — note each one's transcript size AND turn count as it finishes; the first finisher sets the expected duration; absent siblings, cap at 70 MB. | POLL EVERY 5 MINUTES ON TRANSCRIPT BYTES, NOT WALL-CLOCK: `for f in "$TRANSCRIPT_DIR"/agent-*.jsonl; do sz=$(stat -c%s "$f"); [ "$sz" -gt "$CAP" ] && echo "SUSPECT: $(basename $f) $((sz/1024/1024))MB"; done` — trip on either: over the cap, or more than 3x the median sibling. | INTERROGATE ON A TRIP (SendMessage), never wait blind and never kill blind: 'Status check, answer only this: how many items have you completed, how many have you written to <output file>, which batch are you on, and which item are you reading right now?' Circling = same items read again, nothing appended since the last check, a plan restated, or an answer with no number; progress = a rising written-count and a new item id. | HANDLE: circling -> TaskStop, keep what it wrote, relaunch the remainder on a cheaper instrument with a batch cadence; slow but advancing -> let it run, record the revised ETA, poll again; uncertain -> one more interval, and if the written-count has not moved between two checks treat it as circling. Kill early. | PREVENTION, issued VERBATIM to every worker with the values filled: 'Work in batches of about [N] items. For each batch: read the [N], write results for every id, and append to [output file] before starting the next batch. Never read your whole list before writing anything. Read each item exactly once. Report items read, batches used, and reads per item.' N=1 FOR TIMED RUNS (each is >= 6 min and a candidate+control pair is >= 13 min), N=12 for cheap items (file reads, log extractions). The store generator is the sanctioned slow item: it reports bytes written to a named progress file every 60 s and is judged on that counter. An agent that has produced no artifact is NOT 'still working'.
operating_mode.scoreboard: Maintain .goal/srsvd-ooc-throughput.scoreboard.tsv on disk — tab-separated, APPEND-ONLY, header verbatim: `iter\tcandidate_id\tagent\tbranch\tcommit\tartifact\tcommand\tpredicted\tmeasured\tcontrol\tdelta_vs_champion\trecord\trun_id\tprovenance\tnote`. `commit` holds BOTH SHAs as lib@<sha>+bench@<sha>; `measured` and `control` are STEADY5_GB; `run_id` is <slurm job id>/<node>/<GPU UUID short>; `predicted` is copied from the ledger and never edited after the fact; `record` is Y only on the row that became champion (at most one per iteration; the latest Y IS the champion); `provenance` verified/inherited/inferred as in the claims file; `note` carries eligibility labels (numerics-affecting, diagnostic-ineligible, pre-H2, pipelined, NULL-below-floor, FAILED-<reason>, new-allocation). One row per MEASURED candidate; iteration 1 adds the origin rows (one per fresh process). NEVER rewrite or delete a past row — a correction is a NEW row whose note names the row it supersedes. Print the FULL scoreboard in a fenced block at the end of every turn, with the champion identified beneath it by iteration, commit SHAs, flags and STEADY5_GB, and the origin's median STEADY5_GB and the current factor over it.
operating_mode.budget: Delegate 2 to 4 subagents per iteration — ONE TO THREE implementers (opus, xhigh) plus ONE runner — in a regular iteration. The SETUP PHASE is iterations 1-3 at most (declared SETUP in the ledger; it holds the allocation, generates the store on /lscratch, screens cards, builds H1, measures the origin, the noise floor, the tier table and the time budget) and may delegate 1 to 4 workers of any shape and add no candidate; the first iteration after an allocation expires or a node changes may likewise use up to 4. At most ONE exclusive ada allocation live at a time; a replacement may be REQUESTED (pending) when the live one has under 2 h left. Up to FOUR live bridge sessions, one per concurrent caller, counting any this campaign did not start; stop every session this campaign starts.

runner_protocol_reference: Allocation: nohup setsid salloc --no-shell --job-name=ooc --account=lcls:prjdat21 --qos=normal --partition=ada --exclusive --mem=0 --time=48:00:00 & ; poll squeue; print AllocTRES and the wait.
Steps: srun --jobid=<id> --ntasks=1 --gres=gpu:10 ... with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=GPU-<uuid>; print jax.default_backend()=='gpu' and jax.devices() every run.

Per allocation: screen ten cards (UUID, volatile+aggregate ECC), pick the record card, both-precision matmul check, print AllocTRES/memory.max/RealMemory/versions; regenerate the store on /lscratch/ooc/stores/ with the fixed params, print gen output + df -Th + ratio + three slice sha256; run the gate on the champion once and a degraded control; re-measure the champion once.

Per iteration: install candidate SHAs into $W/.venv-cand (--reinstall --no-deps, explicit @sha, both packages), print both direct_url.json from inside the job; run the candidate with --steady-window-s 300 (nvidia-smi sampled every 5 s by UUID); run the champion control from $W/.venv-champ; write each STEADY5-ROW + full log into work/srsvd-ooc-results/iterNN/ and commit after EACH run (batch size 1).
Report REAL MEASURED RESULTS ONLY; never fix the candidate; report what was NOT measured.
implementer_protocol_reference: Branch ooc-throughput off whole-job in work/srsvd-jax and work/srsvd-jax-bench; one candidate per iteration; commit + push; return both SHAs, git status --porcelain, git show --stat, the patch, the exact bench command, predicted STEADY5_GB and the mechanism (which time-budget term), and what was NOT done.

Setup phase (iterations 1-3 at most): harness H1 only (window, block-confirmation timestamps, in-process job loop, STEADY5-ROW printer, --steady-window-s, nvidia-smi hook) on top of whole-job HEAD; no other change, so the origin is whole-job code under H1.

One to three implementers per iteration: separate candidates (own id, prediction, commit; sequential commits through an explicit gate) or one large candidate split by disjoint file ownership with a named integrator landing the single commit.
Never run the experiment; never report a score.
